UnitStatement: Section heading: Telemetry Policy.
This policy defines the OpenPipeStress telemetry posture for DEL-12-03.
The telemetry policy is a privacy and product-boundary artifact, not a telemetry implementation.
The telemetry policy is not a vendor selection, cloud-service design, or professional engineering approval.
The telemetry policy is not a security certification or compliance attestation.
The policy makes no claim that analysis results are fit for reliance without competent human review.
Section heading: Scope.
OpenPipeStress is local-first by default.
The MVP may remain a telemetry no-op.
No telemetry transport, endpoint, vendor, background upload job, queue, or telemetry persistence is required or authorized by this policy.
If telemetry is ever implemented, it must be opt-in only, privacy-preserving, and bounded by a human-approved event allowlist.
Installing the software, opening a project, accepting general terms, importing data, running a solve, exporting a report, or loading a plugin does not constitute telemetry consent.
Section heading: Default-Off Semantics.
Telemetry is disabled by default.
Absent, unset, empty, unknown, unsupported, or malformed telemetry configuration resolves to disabled.

Fail-closed behavior is required: the application must not infer consent from ambiguous configuration, legacy configuration, environment defaults, plugin metadata, import/export settings, or runtime errors.
The exact product configuration schema, storage location, consent UI, endpoint, vendor, retention policy, transport, and concrete event schema remain TBD pending separate human approval.
Section heading: Initialization Rules.

Telemetry must not initialize network transport, background upload jobs, upload queues, local telemetry persistence, endpoints, vendors, or external service clients unless all required conditions are true.
Initialization condition: the user has explicitly opted in through an approved product surface.
Initialization condition: a human-approved event allowlist exists for the exact product version.
Initialization condition: payload filtering is active before any event is constructed.
Initialization condition: protected-content, private-data, secret, and professional-boundary checks are available for telemetry payload review.
Initialization condition: plugin, adapter, import/export, report, and CLI paths cannot bypass the same opt-in and payload-filtering checks.
If any initialization condition is missing, telemetry remains disabled and any attempted event is dropped locally without network behavior.
Section heading: Event Allowlist Rules.
No event is collectable until it appears in a human-approved allowlist.
An allowlist entry must define the event name, permitted fields, field sensitivity, review date, approving human authority, and reason collection is needed.
Unknown events, unapproved event versions, fields not listed on the allowlist, or fields with unclear sensitivity are rejected before payload construction.
The allowlist may approve only low-sensitivity operational metadata.
The allowlist cannot approve private engineering or code data unless the user explicitly selects a specific payload for a specific support or export action under a separate approved workflow.
Section heading: Metadata-Only Guard Helper.
The core/security/telemetry_policy module provides a metadata-only telemetry guard helper for resolving local telemetry configuration and evaluating event attempts before any payload is built.
The guard helper accepts only telemetry configuration metadata, event names, field names, and field classifications, and returns diagnostics and a decision before payload construction.
The helper is a local privacy guard and implementation-hardening artifact.
The helper does not authorize endpoint, vendor, transport, queue, upload, persistence, or telemetry payload construction.
The helper does not select a consent UI, retention policy, support-bundle workflow, cloud service, or professional review state.
If configuration is absent, empty, unknown, unsupported, or malformed, the helper resolves telemetry to disabled.

If an event name, field name, or field classification is unknown, unapproved, private, protected, secret-like, path-like, hash-like, report-like, or a professional/code-compliance claim, the helper rejects the attempt before payload construction.
Section heading: Forbidden Payload Fields.
Telemetry payloads must not include any of the listed forbidden field classes.

Forbidden payload field class: private project models, including project geometry, node coordinates, element topology, loads, load cases, boundary conditions, support settings, solve results, or project package content.
Forbidden payload field class: code-specific rule data, including owner standards, company design bases, rule formulas, rule thresholds, rule inputs, rule evaluation results, or private rule logic.
Forbidden payload field class: private rule packs, including rule-pack payloads, private rule-pack metadata beyond a user-approved public identifier, private checksums, or private source notes.

Forbidden payload field class: private material or component libraries, including material values, component catalog rows, vendor-derived records, provenance notes, private source references, or library file contents.
Forbidden payload field class: generated reports and exports, including report bodies, templates, attachments, screenshots, exported models, export payloads, or shared-model packages.
Forbidden payload field class: model hashes, including project, manifest, report, rule-pack, or private-library hashes or other identifiers that can fingerprint private work.
Forbidden payload field class: local file paths, including user names, project names embedded in paths, directory names, file names, mount points, repository paths, or temporary paths.
Forbidden payload field class: secrets and credentials, including tokens, passwords, API keys, license keys, certificates, private keys, signing keys, cookies, or authorization headers.

Forbidden payload field class: protected standards content, including standards text, tables, figures, copied examples, copied formulas, proprietary engineering values, commercial benchmark content, or protected/code-derived content.
Forbidden payload field class: professional or code-compliance claims, including claims of certification, sealing, professional approval, code compliance, safety approval, or fitness for reliance.
Section heading: Diagnostics And Reports.
Telemetry diagnostics, if added later, must use the project diagnostic envelope where available and must not include private payload content.
Diagnostics may state that telemetry is disabled, blocked, or rejected, but must not print the rejected private value.
Reports, exports, screenshots, public examples, and bug-report bundles must not include telemetry payloads by default.
Any future support bundle workflow must require explicit attachment review by the user and must preserve the protected-content and private-data boundary.
Section heading: No-Bypass Surfaces.

The telemetry opt-in and payload-filtering rules apply equally to first-party code, plugins, adapters, import/export paths, report generators, private library mechanisms, CLI runners, diagnostics, tests, and future application services.
No plugin manifest, adapter declaration, CLI option, imported file, report template, or rule pack can enable telemetry, add telemetry fields, define an endpoint, or bypass the allowlist by itself.
Section heading: Open Decisions.
Open decision: product configuration schema is TBD; absent, unset, unknown, unsupported, or malformed configuration resolves to disabled.
Open decision: consent UI or CLI surface is TBD; consent must be explicit and distinct from install, terms acceptance, project open, import, solve, export, or plugin load.
Open decision: endpoint, vendor, transport, and retention policy are TBD; no such behavior is authorized by this policy.
Open decision: concrete event schema and event allowlist are TBD; no event is collectable without human-approved allowlist evidence.
Open decision: support bundle or explicit user-selected payload workflow is TBD; no private payload is eligible for automatic telemetry.
Section heading: Verification Expectations.
Verification expectation: traceability to DEL-12-03, PKG-12, SOW-037, and OBJ-010.
Verification expectation: default-off behavior for absent, unset, empty, unknown, unsupported, and malformed configuration.

Verification expectation: no initialization of telemetry transport, endpoints, vendors, upload jobs, upload queues, persistence, or external service clients without explicit opt-in and a human-approved event allowlist.
Verification expectation: rejection of forbidden private-data, protected-content, secret, path, hash, report, and professional-claim fields before payload construction.
Verification expectation: preservation of local-first behavior and no-bypass rules for plugins, adapters, import/export, reports, CLI, diagnostics, and application services.
Verification expectation: explicit TBD markers for configuration schema, consent surface, endpoint, vendor, retention policy, transport, and event schema.

Verification expectation: absence of protected standards content, proprietary engineering values, real private project data, real secrets, and professional/code-compliance or security-certification claims.
